sections.h2: What should I know about selling a house in Egg Harbor Township, NJ?
sections.html:
Egg Harbor Township is a large Atlantic County municipality, 75.47 square miles of which 67.05 is land, and it is separate from Egg Harbor City, which has its own entry in the state's municipality lists. The Census Bureau estimates 48,435 residents for 2025. Owner-occupancy is high at 84.4 percent, the median owner-occupied home value is $312,700, and median household income is $97,190.

Those figures make the township the lowest-priced of four New Jersey towns covered in this series, with the largest share of homeowners. For a seller that means most buyers are other families buying a primary residence, and the sale rests on a state fire-safety certificate, not a township resale inspection.

sections.h2: Does Egg Harbor Township require a smoke and carbon monoxide certificate?
sections.html:
New Jersey's Division of Fire Safety runs an online smoke certification application with "Change of Ownership" as a stated reason, and it asks for the closing date, block, lot and whether you are the seller or the buyer's representative. Sheriff's sales, foreclosures, forfeitures and purchases from a federal agency work differently: the new owner must obtain the certificate before moving in. A building that is uninhabitable and will be rehabilitated or demolished can be exempt from the certificate, but it cannot be occupied until a new certificate of occupancy comes from the local construction official.

For the township's own form, fee and timing, ask the Bureau of Fire Inspections before you set a closing date. Replace missing alarms before you apply, because the inspection looks at every sleeping area and level.

sections.h2: How did the township get its shape?
sections.html:
Lenape families summered near Bargaintown Lake and along Patcong Creek. A 1694 act placed the Egg Harbour settlers under Gloucester County, and Atlantic County was separated in 1837. Since then, ten municipalities have split from the original township, among them Atlantic City in 1854, Somers Point in 1886 and Ventnor City in 1903.

What remains is spread out. The seat of government is in Bargaintown, and the township includes Cardiff, English Creek, Farmington, Scullville, Steelmanville and West Atlantic City, plus part of McKee City. West Atlantic City and Anchorage Poynte are not contiguous with the main body. A listing should name the section, because buyers search by those names.

sections.h2: How do the Pinelands rules affect a house here?
sections.html:
The township is one of 56 South Jersey municipalities in the Pinelands National Reserve, and part of it lies in the state-designated Pinelands Area. The Pinelands Commission classed Egg Harbor Township, Hamilton and Galloway as Regional Growth Areas, which pushed residential building here so that trees in the preserved Pine Barrens stay standing.

  • That designation is why newer subdivisions such as the planned Village at Farmington were approved with townhouses, age-restricted homes and single-family houses.
  • If your lot sits near wetlands or protected land, ask the township's construction office about limits before planning a deck, shed or addition.
  • Wildlife management areas including Malibu Beach, Pork Island and Lester G. MacNamara are public land that borders private property in the south and east.

sections.h2: What does the township offer commuters and families?
sections.html:
The Atlantic City Expressway crosses the township for 5.3 miles and meets the Garden State Parkway at Interchange 7, which is Parkway Interchange 38. The Parkway runs 8.6 miles through, and Routes 40, 322 and 9 plus county routes 559, 563, 575 and 585 carry local traffic. NJ Transit buses 502, 507, 508 and 509 link the township with Atlantic City. Most of Atlantic City International Airport lies in the northern part of the township, so airport noise and access are part of the picture for houses nearby. The Census puts mean travel to work at 23.3 minutes, the shortest of the four towns.

The township has 297 miles of roads, 207 of them municipal. Harbor Square, the former Shore Mall, is the regional shopping center, and the Atlantic County Bikeway runs 7.5 miles from the mall toward Hamilton Township.

sections.h2: Which schools serve Egg Harbor Township homes?
sections.html: Egg Harbor Township Schools run seven schools for pre-kindergarten through grade 12. The 2023-24 enrollment was 7,473 students with a 10.9 to 1 student-teacher ratio. Davenport and Swift-Slaybaugh serve the early grades, the Dr. Joyanne D. Miller school takes grades 4 and 5, Alder Avenue and Fernwood Avenue are the middle schools, and Egg Harbor Township High School had 2,299 students. Students can also go to the Atlantic County Institute of Technology in Mays Landing or the Charter-Tech High School for the Performing Arts in Somers Point.

sections.h2: What do the state's transfer fees look like for a typical Egg Harbor Township sale?
sections.html:
With a median value of $312,700, most township sales fall in the state's lower schedule for deals up to $350,000.

Source: NJ Division of Taxation. The state's worked example puts the fee at $1,910 on a $325,000 deed with no exemption. Seniors, blind or disabled sellers and low or moderate income housing qualify for a partial exemption using Form RTF-1.

sections.h2: How do I appeal an assessment or record a deed in Atlantic County?
sections.html:
Atlantic County's Board of Taxation sits in Mays Landing at 5909 Main Street and can be reached at (609) 645-5820. Petitions are due by April 1, and hearings usually run April through September at the Historic Courthouse. The board mails a hearing notice at least ten days ahead, and any comparable sales you rely on must reach the board, the municipal assessor and the municipal clerk at least seven days before the hearing. Good comparables are real sales in the same town within the year before the prior October 1; most foreclosures, sheriff's sales, estate sales and short sales are treated as not usable. A reduction comes back as a credit through a revised bill from the tax collector, and you have 45 days from the judgment to go to the State Tax Court.

A resident seller signs GIT/REP-3 for the deed. Nonresidents use GIT/REP-1 or GIT/REP-2 unless a listed assurance applies.

faqs.q: Is Egg Harbor Township the same as Egg Harbor City?
faqs.a: No. The state lists Egg Harbor Township and Egg Harbor City as separate municipalities. This page covers the township, which had 48,435 residents in the 2025 Census estimate.

faqs.q: Do I need a smoke and CO certificate to sell in Egg Harbor Township?
faqs.a: Yes, a change of ownership calls for a state smoke and carbon monoxide certificate. Ask the township's Bureau of Fire Inspections for its form, fee and timing before you pick a closing date.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Egg Harbor Township?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau reports $312,700 for owner-occupied homes in the 2020 to 2024 period, and 84.4 percent of homes are owner occupied.

faqs.q: When is the Atlantic County tax appeal deadline?
faqs.a: April 1 of the tax year, filed with the Atlantic County Board of Taxation. Where a revaluation was done, the deadline is May 1.

faqs.q: How long are Atlantic County hearing notices sent in advance?
faqs.a: At least ten days before the hearing. Comparable sales evidence is due to the board, the assessor and the clerk at least seven days before.
